Found the file change — it was in `AlarmsManager.java` at that commit (later renamed to `Alarms.java`), which is why plain `git log --follow` on the renamed path didn't surface it directly.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: f1939c88e3f8602b993b1b2e30bda8b4adb34409

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit (62dd6a1) changes `init()`'s loop that disables expired alarms — instead of calling `enable(alarm.getId(), false)` (which internally called `changeAlarm()`, which mutated the in-memory `set` via `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);`), it now calls `alarm.setEnabled(false); writeToDb(alarm.getId());` directly, bypassing the set mutation. This is the classic pattern of a `ConcurrentModificationException`: the loop does `for (Alarm alarm : set) { ... enable(...) ... }` while `enable()` transitively removes/re-adds elements from that same `set` being iterated.

I traced the history of this file (`Alarms.java`, formerly `AlarmsManager.java`) using `git log -p --follow` to find when this loop-over-`set`-while-mutating-`set` pattern was introduced.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `f1939c88` (Jul 22, 2012) refactored `AlarmsManager` to cache alarms in an in-memory `Set<Alarm> set` field (previously alarms were always read fresh from a `Cursor`/`ContentResolver` query). As part of this refactor:
- `disableExpiredAlarms()` was changed from iterating over a `Cursor` to iterating over the in-memory `set`, while still calling `enable(alarm.getId(), false)` inside the loop.
- `enable()` calls `changeAlarm()`, which was newly introduced in this same commit and does `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);` — mutating the very set being iterated.

Before this commit, `disableExpiredAlarms()` iterated over a `Cursor` from a fresh DB query, so calling `enable()`/`set()` (which only touched the DB, not any in-memory collection) was safe. After this commit, the loop and the mutation target the same live `Set<Alarm>` object, producing a `ConcurrentModificationException` whenever an expired, disabled alarm was found during `init()`.

This same unsafe pattern persisted through later refactors (e.g., `717ab02` inlined `disableExpiredAlarms()` into `init()` but kept calling `enable()` inside the `for (Alarm alarm : set)` loop) until it was finally fixed in `62dd6a1` by avoiding the `set.remove/set.add` round-trip in that code path.

**(3) Supporting evidence:**
- `git show f1939c88 -- src/com/better/alarm/model/AlarmsManager.java` shows the field `private Set<Alarm> set;` being added, `disableExpiredAlarms()` changed to `for (Alarm alarm : set) { ... enable(alarm.getId(), false); }`, and the new `changeAlarm()` method containing `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);`.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor f1939c88... HEAD` confirms this commit is in the ancestry of the bug-fix commit on `subject-bfc`.
- The fix in `62dd6a1` directly targets this exact loop/mutation interaction, replacing the `enable()` call (which triggers `set.remove/add`) with a direct field mutation + DB write that doesn't touch `set`, confirming that the set-mutation-during-iteration was the root cause being fixed.

I'm fairly confident in this identification since the fix's mechanism (avoiding set mutation during iteration) maps precisely onto the pattern introduced in `f1939c88`. The main uncertainty is stylistic: one could argue `717ab02` (which moved the loop into `init()` but kept the same unsafe call) is also "where the bug most recently manifested in this exact code," but the underlying defect — iterating a live `Set` while a called method mutates that same `Set` — was introduced in `f1939c88`, not reintroduced or newly created by `717ab02`.
